dedupe_keys.name: report for machine learning driven near surface velocity modelling in the north sea using onshore data to predict offshore conditions

description: Report for "Machine learning-driven, near-surface velocity modelling in the North Sea: Using onshore data to predict offshore conditions" is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Morgan Sanger, University of Washington (washington.edu). Shear-wave velocity (Vs) is an essential parameter in evaluating geotechnical hazards and in foundation design. Conventional techniques to measure Vs are time-intensive, costly, and infeasible to perform at high resolution across large sites such as offshore wind farms. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (TIF, PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-jxga-6486. Keywords: machine learning, shear-wave velocity, offshore wind farms, North Sea, site classification. Published 2026-04-13. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
